### 1. What the user expresses; simulator behaviour

- Target object: "I have a payment plan with you" — the caller's payment arrangement (one Lakeshore Federal card account).
- Action: "I want the payments to come out of my debit card automatically every month from now on" → a payment-method change to automatic card debit (`funding_method` = `card_autopay`, per the schema/KB enum "card_autopay (installments charged automatically to a debit or credit card)").
- Timing: "from now on" — the next installment the new method can collect.
- Authorisation mode: script — "if the agent mentions an electronic signature, you say you would rather just give your OK right here on this recorded call" → `recorded_call`. KB matrix: Standard Installment Plan "Recorded telephone authorization suffices: Yes"; desk guide "A payment-method change ... takes effect on the consumer's new authorization, given the same way as at set-up" and plan record `authorization_method: 'recorded_call'`.
- Simulator is passive: identity details only when asked; reason (closed old checking account) only if asked; "If the agent tells you that something on the plan has to be adjusted first ... you say that is fine"; executes the user-owned tool exactly as read out. It does not raise the returned payment or any re-dating itself.

### 4. Scored parameters — formula, inputs, factor tiers, values

**(a) Re-dating shift (`redate_returned_installment_ce690b15.shift_days`), installment 7.**
Computation doc (redating_shift_calculation): shift = calendar days from the scheduled due date carried on the most recent returned installment payment to the new due date; new due date = clock start advanced by lead + verification buffer; capped at the type's largest shift (Standard 15). Factor documents found from the records:
- Clock start (redating_clock_start): most recent return reason `account_closed`, due 2026-10-06, received 2026-10-07, lag 1 day ≤ Standard automatic-debit grace 5 → "the re-dating clock starts on the date the return was received" = **2026-10-07 (Wed)**. Led there by the record words "returned", "account_closed", return date.
- Lead (redating_lead_and_payment_record): kept installment payments = 8 payment entries − 1 returned entry = 7 ≥ 6; other returned installment payments in last 12 months besides the most recent: none → **3 days**. Led by the count of paid/returned entries on the installment history.
- Verification buffer (redating_verification_buffer): returned payments on the placed account "that carry no payment plan reference" within 12 whole months back from 2026-10-09: the check returned 2026-02-17, reason stop_payment → clause (a) **2 days**. Led by the account money-history row `account_payment_returned`, `check_by_mail`, `plan_id None`, `stop_payment` (Placed Consumer Accounts records).
- Day-count convention (redating_day_count_conventions): channel of the most recent returned installment payment `ach_bank_debit` → "counted in business days, Monday to Friday, after the clock start, the clock start itself not counted". 3 + 2 = 5 business days after Wed 2026-10-07: Thu 8, Fri 9, Mon 12, Tue 13, Wed 14 → **2026-10-14**.
- Shift: 2026-10-06 → 2026-10-14 = **8** days; 8 ≤ 15, no cap.
- Fall-back (computation document alone: clock = handling date 2026-10-09, lead 7, buffer 0, calendar days, cap 15): 2026-10-16, shift **10** — definite and different from 8.

**(b) First installment collected by the new method (`authorize_payment_method_50f022be.installment_number`).**
Computation doc (first_collected_installment_calculation): covered = payments received − returned − down payment + type tolerance = (114 + 197×6 + 194 = 1490.00) − 197.00 − 114.00 + 5.00 (Standard tolerance) = 1184.00; 1184.00 / 197.00 = 6.01 → 6 whole → hand-over next installment **7**, which is the installment of the most recent returned installment payment. Rule: the new method collects it only if it is the schedule anchor installment and days from the handling date to the schedule anchor date > set-up notice + extension + return allowance; otherwise installment 8.
After the due-date change, the plan's schedule anchor is installment 7 at 2026-10-14 (redate tool: "it becomes the schedule anchor installment with that new due date"; confirmed by a simulated find_payment_plans after the write: `schedule_anchor_installment 7`, `schedule_anchor_date 2026-10-14`).
Factor documents found from the records:
- Set-up notice (setup_notice_by_payment_record): kept 7 ≥ 6, no missed installment recorded in last 12 months → **3 days**.
- Set-up notice extension (setup_notice_extension_card_history): debit-card payment 194.00 posted 2026-07-02 on the consumer's placed account (money history `payment_channel debit_card`), no card return, no payment-method change on this plan → clause (a) **0 days**. Led by the debit_card row.
- Return allowance (setup_notice_return_allowance): kept 7 ≥ 6; no other returned installment payment within 6 months besides the most recent → **0 days**.
- Day count (setup_notice_day_count): most recent returned installment payment reason `account_closed` → calendar days: 2026-10-09 → 2026-10-14 = **5**.
- 5 > 3 + 0 + 0 = 3 → the new method first collects installment **7** (due 2026-10-14).
- Fall-back (computation doc alone, after the same due-date change): threshold 5 + 2 + 2 = 9; business days after Fri 2026-10-09 to Wed 2026-10-14 = 3; 3 ≤ 9 → installment **8** — definite and different from 7.

**(c) Other arguments.** `plan_id` bfd361fc-a9a6-4fa7-b33a-aa11c7086b17; `funding_method` card_autopay; `authorization_method` recorded_call.

### 6. Problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

Problems: P1 = payment-method change (customer's request, root, user-owned write); P2 = re-dating of the returned installment 7 (agent write). Direction: P1 waits on P2. Order: P2 → P1.

- Hop P1 → P2 — **state-derived**.
  - Visible sentence on P1's hub (new_payment_method_authorization): "The first installment a newly authorized payment method collects is fixed only after the plan's installment history carries a due-date change for the installment of its most recent returned installment payment." (and its same-form restatement "while the installment history shows no due-date change … the number of the first installment the new method collects is not yet fixed").
  - Query: `find_plan_installments` → most recent returned installment payment is installment 7 (account_closed, 2026-10-07); no `change_type` due-date entry exists → state unmet.
  - Searching the state's words ("due-date change", "returned installment") finds returned_installment_redating: "the installment that payment was for is re-dated by one due-date change … recorded once on the plan's installment history against the returned payment's installment", tool `redate_returned_installment_ce690b15`. Its applicability: "An installment payment returned for account closed, stop payment, unauthorized debit or card chargeback is never presented again" — the return reason is account_closed → applicable.
  - Combination: P2's write produces exactly the waited-on entry; P2 itself carries no prerequisite sentence on its hub → tree ends.
- No other prerequisite appears on P1's or P2's documents; the account block condition is a gate (not met → nothing to resolve).

### Two-way counter-proof

- Support: every value above rests on quoted visible sentences and query rows.
- Closest alternatives excluded:
  - clock start on handling date / due date: excluded by redating_clock_start row "Account closed or stop payment | Not more than the grace period | The date the return was received" (lag 1 ≤ 5);
  - calendar-day counting for the re-date: excluded by day-count convention row "ACH bank debit | Business days … after the clock start";
  - buffer 0 because the stop-payment check is "not a plan payment": excluded — clause counts exactly the returned payments "that carry no payment plan reference";
  - business-day count for the set-up notice: excluded by setup_notice_day_count "After a return for account closed or stop payment, the days … are counted in calendar days";
  - `e_signature`: excluded by matrix (Standard accepts recorded telephone) + persona refusing e-signature;
  - `ach_autopay`/`manual_pay`: excluded by the request (debit card automatic).
- "Do only the one thing asked" (authorize the card right away): excluded by the state-form prerequisite sentence — without a due-date change for installment 7 "the number of the first installment the new method collects is not yet fixed"; also, without it the plan's anchor installment is 1, so the computation would hand the card installment 8 and leave installment 7 (whose ACH return "is never presented again") uncollected.
- Calculation fall-backs (recorded above): shift 10 vs 8; first installment 8 vs 7. Each factor reached from record words (return reason/date, payment/return counts, off-plan returned check with no plan reference, debit_card payment row, ACH channel); none reached through the computation document's wording alone, although the computation documents name the components (lead, buffer, set-up notice extension, return allowance) with default values.
